Actions on Objectives

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

[LLM] Network egress to OFAC-sanctioned Iranian crypto exchanges (Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, Ramzinex) Command & Control High
Hunts for DNS / HTTP / proxy traffic from corporate endpoints to the four Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges (Nobitex.ir, Wallex.ir, Bitpin.ir, Ramzinex.com) designated by OFAC on 2026-06-03 under the 'Economic Fury' campaign. Any U.S.-jurisdiction host reaching these domains creates an immediate sanctions-compliance event, and may also surface IRGC-affiliated ransomware operators routing payments through Nobitex. Rationale: Uses the four exchange domains pre-extracted from the article (Nobitex.ir, Wallex.ir, Bitpin.ir, Ramzinex.com — note article typo 'Rumzinex.com' is also covered). These are not generic threat-hunting indicators — they map to a specific OFAC SDN designation issued 2026-06-03 under the 'Economic Fury' campaign, so any U.S.-jurisdiction contact is itself the violation. Cross-checked: Treasury press release referenced in body, and Chainalysis 2025 Iran crypto ecosystem figures (~$7.8B inflow, Nobitex >50%) used to scope criticality. The article also cites the 2025 Predatory Sparrow breach of Nobitex, confirming the exchange's role as IRGC-linked ransomware payment infrastructure. Cross-checked against: • https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/financial-sanctions/recent-actions • https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/iran-crypto-ecosystem-2025/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1657/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1657
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let SanctionedDomains = dynamic(["nobitex.ir","wallex.ir","bitpin.ir","ramzinex.com","rumzinex.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (SanctionedDomains)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let SanctionedDomains = dynamic(["nobitex.ir","wallex.ir","bitpin.ir","ramzinex.com","rumzinex.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (SanctionedDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = coalesce(SrcHostname, DvcHostname), SrcIp = SrcIpAddr, User = SrcUsername, Indicator = DnsQuery, Source = "DNS"
),
(
  ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Url has_any (SanctionedDomains) or HttpHostName has_any (SanctionedDomains) or DstHostname has_any (SanctionedDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = coalesce(SrcHostname, DvcHostname), SrcIp = SrcIpAddr, User = SrcUsername, Indicator = coalesce(Url, HttpHostName, DstHostname), Source = "Web"
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has_any (SanctionedDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (SanctionedDomains) or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (SanctionedDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, SrcIp = SourceIP, User = SourceUserName, Indicator = coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain), Source = "Proxy"
),
(
  DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Name has_any (SanctionedDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, SrcIp = ClientIP, User = "", Indicator = Name, Source = "WinDNS"
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DNS / Web Connection to OFAC-Sanctioned Iranian Crypto Exchange (2026 Economic Fury)
id: 7c5d2f1b-9a83-4e6a-8f2d-1c5b9f3e7a4d
description: Detects DNS resolution or web traffic to the four Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges (Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, Ramzinex) designated by OFAC on 2026-06-03 for facilitating IRGC-linked ransomware payments and sanctions evasion. Any contact from a U.S.-jurisdiction host is a sanctions-compliance event.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/the-us-sanctions-nobitex-crypto-exchange-used-by-ransomware/
  - https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/financial-sanctions/recent-actions
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1071.004
  - attack.t1657
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith:
      - nobitex.ir
      - wallex.ir
      - bitpin.ir
      - ramzinex.com
      - rumzinex.com
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Sanctioned-trade compliance / treasury research teams with documented business need
  - Threat intelligence researchers actively profiling Iranian crypto infrastructure
  - Security-vendor crawlers (VirusTotal, urlscan, abuse.ch) operating from corporate IP space
level: high
(@dns.question.name:(*nobitex.ir OR *wallex.ir OR *bitpin.ir OR *ramzinex.com OR *rumzinex.com) OR @network.destination.domain:(nobitex.ir OR wallex.ir OR bitpin.ir OR ramzinex.com OR rumzinex.com) OR @http.url_details.host:(nobitex.ir OR wallex.ir OR bitpin.ir OR ramzinex.com OR rumzinex.com) OR @QueryName:(*nobitex.ir OR *wallex.ir OR *bitpin.ir OR *ramzinex.com OR *rumzinex.com) OR @DestinationHostname:(*nobitex.ir OR *wallex.ir OR *bitpin.ir OR *ramzinex.com OR *rumzinex.com))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)(nobitex\.ir|wallex\.ir|bitpin\.ir|ramzinex\.com|rumzinex\.com)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName], function=[count(as=Hits), min(@timestamp, as=FirstSeen), max(@timestamp, as=LastSeen)])
| sort(LastSeen, order=desc)
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url IN ("*nobitex.ir*","*wallex.ir*","*bitpin.ir*","*ramzinex.com*","*rumzinex.com*") OR Web.dest IN ("*nobitex.ir","*wallex.ir","*bitpin.ir","*ramzinex.com","*rumzinex.com")) by Web.src Web.user Web.dest Web.url Web.http_user_agent Web.http_method | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | append [ | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query IN ("*nobitex.ir","*wallex.ir","*bitpin.ir","*ramzinex.com","*rumzinex.com") by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.answer | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | rename query as dest ] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url IN ("*nobitex.ir*","*wallex.ir*","*bitpin.ir*","*ramzinex.com*","*rumzinex.com*") OR Web.dest IN ("*nobitex.ir","*wallex.ir","*bitpin.ir","*ramzinex.com","*rumzinex.com")) by Web.src Web.user Web.dest Web.url Web.http_user_agent Web.http_method | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | append [ | tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query IN ("*nobitex.ir","*wallex.ir","*bitpin.ir","*ramzinex.com","*rumzinex.com") by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.answer | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | rename query as dest ] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:

level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

New 'HTTP/2 Bomb' DoS attack crashes web servers in under a minute

BleepingComputer
2026-06-03 4 use cases 1 technique 5 kill-chain phases detected

A new denial-of-service (DoS) attack dubbed HTTP/2 Bomb can be launched from a single machine to take down web servers within seconds. [...]

CVEsCVE-2026-49975
ATT&CKT1190
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix
Phase 1

Detected

Weaponization
Detected
Phase 3

Phase 4
Exploitation
Detected
Phase 5

Phase 6
Command & Control
Detected
Phase 7
Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Vulnerable HTTP/2 server inventory (CVE-2026-49975 — nginx/mod_http2/Envoy/IIS)
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] HTTP/2 Bomb stall signature — long-hung HTTP/2 requests with near-zero response bytes
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Web-tier worker crash / OOM storm following HTTP/2 Bomb memory exhaustion
[LLM] Vulnerable HTTP/2 server inventory (CVE-2026-49975 — nginx/mod_http2/Envoy/IIS) Weaponization High
Surfaces hosts running HTTP/2-capable web servers at versions the Calif researchers proved vulnerable to the HTTP/2 Bomb (nginx pre-1.29.8, Apache httpd with mod_http2 < 2.0.41, Envoy 1.37.2, and IIS on Windows Server 2025 where no patch yet exists). Inventory-based hunt that prioritises patching/HTTP-2-disable work and identifies the attack surface for the follow-up runtime detections. Rationale: Pivots on CveId == CVE-2026-49975 (the assigned identifier from the Apache disclosure) plus the exact vulnerable build strings the article names (nginx 1.29.7, mod_http2 < 2.0.41, Envoy 1.37.2, IIS on Windows Server 2025). Joining DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing focuses triage on hosts the article notes are most exposed — CDN-fronted estates are 'more difficult to target'. Cross-checked against Tenable's CVE record and the upstream nginx commit adding max_headers. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.calif.io/p/codex-discovered-a-hidden-http2-bomb • https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-49975 • https://github.com/nginx/nginx/commit/365694160a85229a7cb006738de9260d49ff5fa2 • https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q2/790
ATT&CKT1190 T1499.003
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
// HTTP/2 Bomb (CVE-2026-49975) — vulnerable HTTP/2 server inventory
let TvmHits =
    DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where CveId == "CVE-2026-49975"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, Source="TVM CVE feed";
let InventoryHits =
    DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    // article names these specific vulnerable builds
    | where (SoftwareName has "nginx"  and SoftwareVersion == "1.29.7")
         or (SoftwareName has "httpd"  and SoftwareVersion startswith "2.4." and SoftwareVersion !in ("2.4.68","2.4.69","2.4.70"))
         or (SoftwareName has "mod_http2" and SoftwareVersion startswith "2.0." and SoftwareVersion < "2.0.41")
         or (SoftwareName has "envoy" and SoftwareVersion == "1.37.2")
         or (SoftwareName has "IIS"   and OSVersion has "Windows Server 2025")
    | extend CveId="CVE-2026-49975", Source="Inventory match"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, Source;
union TvmHits, InventoryHits
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP) by DeviceId, DeviceName) on DeviceName

[LLM] HTTP/2 Bomb stall signature — long-hung HTTP/2 requests with near-zero response bytes Command & Control Medium
Detects the zero-window flow-control hold half of the HTTP/2 Bomb: the server has allocated memory but never emits a response because the client advertises a zero-byte WINDOW. On the wire this shows up as small numbers of inbound HTTP/2 requests from a single source IP that each persist for tens of seconds while the server returns almost no bytes. Targets IIS / nginx / Apache / Envoy access logs and inbound network telemetry. Rationale: Encodes the exact wire signature the article describes: 'requests are never fully completed, and the allocated memory keeps growing' via zero-byte WINDOW + tiny WINDOW_UPDATE responses. TimeTaken ≥ 20s with scBytes ≤ 1024 captures Apache/Envoy 32-GB-in-20s and IIS 64-GB-in-45s profiles. Few-but-long (HungReqs ≥ 3) — not a flood — matches Calif's 'single-client' claim. Cross-checked against the Calif technical write-up (blog.calif.io) and SecurityWeek's reproduction summary. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.calif.io/p/codex-discovered-a-hidden-http2-bomb • https://www.securityweek.com/http-2-bomb-exploit-knocks-web-servers-offline-in-seconds/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-http2-bomb-vulnerability-allows.html
ATT&CKT1499.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
// HTTP/2 Bomb stall signature — multiple held inbound HTTP/2 connections from a single source
let WebProcs = dynamic(["nginx.exe","httpd.exe","w3wp.exe","envoy.exe","iisexpress.exe","apache2","nginx","httpd"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| where ActionType =~ "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where LocalPort in (443, 8443, 80)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any (WebProcs)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"        // ignore intra-DC health checks
| summarize ConnCount       = count(),
            DistinctRemotePorts = dcount(RemotePort),
            FirstConn        = min(Timestamp),
            LastConn         = max(Timestamp),
            HoldSeconds      = datetime_diff('second', max(Timestamp), min(Timestamp))
        by DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where ConnCount >= 20 and HoldSeconds >= 20    // 20+ simultaneous inbound h2 conns held ≥20s — matches Apache/Envoy 32GB-in-20s profile
| project FirstConn, LastConn, DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, ConnCount, DistinctRemotePorts, HoldSeconds
| order by ConnCount desc
// HTTP/2 Bomb stall — IIS/web access logs showing held requests with near-zero response
let IISHung =
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
    | where TimeTaken >= 20000           // ≥20s — article: 32GB consumed in ~20s on Apache/Envoy
    | where scBytes  <= 1024             // server emitted no real response body
    | where csMethod !in~ ("PUT","POST") or csBytes < 65536   // exclude legitimate slow large uploads
    | summarize HungReqs = count(),
                DistinctUris = dcount(csUriStem),
                TotalHoldMs = sum(TimeTaken),
                MaxHoldMs   = max(TimeTaken),
                SampleAgent = any(csUserAgent),
                FirstSeen   = min(TimeGenerated),
                LastSeen    = max(TimeGenerated)
            by cIP, sSiteName, Computer
    | where HungReqs >= 3                // bomb is FEW long streams, not a flood
    | project FirstSeen, LastSeen, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, HungReqs, DistinctUris, MaxHoldMs, TotalHoldMs, SampleAgent;
let AsimHung =
    ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
    | where NetworkDuration >= 20000
    | where HttpResponseBodyBytes <= 1024
    | summarize HungReqs = count(),
                TotalHoldMs = sum(NetworkDuration),
                MaxHoldMs   = max(NetworkDuration),
                DistinctUris = dcount(Url),
                FirstSeen   = min(TimeGenerated),
                LastSeen    = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcIpAddr, DvcHostname
    | where HungReqs >= 3
    | project FirstSeen, LastSeen, Computer=DvcHostname, sSiteName="", cIP=SrcIpAddr, HungReqs, DistinctUris, MaxHoldMs, TotalHoldMs, SampleAgent="";
union IISHung, AsimHung
| order by MaxHoldMs desc
(source:iis OR source:nginx.access OR source:apache.access) @http.method:* (@duration:>=20000 OR @time_taken:>=20000) (@http.response_content_length:<1024 OR @sc_bytes:<1024 OR @network.bytes_written:<1024) -@http.url_details.path:(/healthz OR /ping OR /events OR /stream OR /sse OR /ws OR /websocket)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ConnectionDirection=1
| ContextImageFileName=/(nginx|httpd|w3wp|envoy|apache2)(\.exe)?$/i
| RemotePort=/^(443|8443|80)$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4, ContextImageFileName], function=count(), limit=1000)
| count >= 20
# log group: /aws/applicationelb/access-logs   (or wherever your ALB access logs flow into CWLI)
fields @timestamp, client_ip, target_processing_time, request_processing_time, response_processing_time, sent_bytes, received_bytes, request_url, elb_status_code, protocol
| filter protocol = "HTTP/2"
      and target_processing_time >= 20
      and sent_bytes <= 1024
      and request_url not like /(\/healthz|\/ping|\/sse|\/events|\/stream|\/ws)/i
| stats count(*) as hung_reqs, max(target_processing_time) as max_hold, sum(sent_bytes) as total_sent by client_ip, request_url
| filter hung_reqs >= 3
| sort max_hold desc

[LLM] Web-tier worker crash / OOM storm following HTTP/2 Bomb memory exhaustion Actions on Objectives High
Detects the impact phase: rapid worker-process recycles or OOM-killer events on hosts running nginx, Apache httpd, IIS (w3wp.exe), or Envoy. The HTTP/2 Bomb causes 32–64 GB of RAM to be consumed in 10–45 seconds; on Linux this triggers oom-killer; on Windows IIS this triggers Application Pool crash-recycles and Application Error 1000 events naming w3wp.exe. Designed to fire even if the on-wire UC2 missed the request shape. Rationale: Built directly on the article's impact description — 32–64 GB RAM exhaustion in 10–45 seconds. On Linux this surfaces as oom-killer entries naming nginx/httpd/envoy in Syslog; on Windows IIS the bomb crash-loops the application pool, producing Application Error 1000 events naming w3wp.exe plus rapid 4688 NewProcessName=w3wp.exe spawns. Pivots on web-server binary names from the article's tested versions. Cross-checked against the Calif technical write-up and the oss-sec disclosure. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.calif.io/p/codex-discovered-a-hidden-http2-bomb • https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q2/790 • https://gbhackers.com/http-2-bomb-remote-dos-exploit/
ATT&CKT1499.003 T1499.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// HTTP/2 Bomb impact — web worker restart storm (process pool churn from OOM)
let WebProcs = dynamic(["nginx.exe","httpd.exe","apache2","httpd","w3wp.exe","envoy.exe","nginx"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| where FileName in~ WebProcs or FileName has_any (WebProcs)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize SpawnCount    = count(),
            DistinctPids  = dcount(ProcessId),
            FirstSpawn    = min(Timestamp),
            LastSpawn     = max(Timestamp),
            SampleParent  = any(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            SampleCmd     = any(ProcessCommandLine)
        by DeviceName, FileName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where SpawnCount >= 10                           // 10 worker (re)starts in 5 min — well above normal recycle rate
| extend StormWindowSec = datetime_diff('second', LastSpawn, FirstSpawn)
| project FirstSpawn, LastSpawn, StormWindowSec, DeviceName, FileName, SpawnCount, DistinctPids, SampleParent, SampleCmd
| order by SpawnCount desc
// HTTP/2 Bomb impact — OOM-killer (Linux) and Application Error 1000 (Windows IIS) targeting web workers
let LookbackHours = 1h;
let LinuxOOM =
    Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where SyslogMessage has "oom-killer" or (SyslogMessage has "Out of memory" and SyslogMessage has "Killed process")
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("nginx","httpd","apache2","envoy")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName="oom-killer", Detail=SyslogMessage, Platform="Linux";
let WinIISCrash =
    Event
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where EventID == 1000 and Source has "Application Error"
    | where RenderedDescription has_any ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","envoy.exe")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName="Application Error 1000", Detail=RenderedDescription, Platform="Windows";
let WinWorkerStorm =
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\w3wp.exe","\\nginx.exe","\\httpd.exe","\\envoy.exe")
    | summarize Spawns=count(), arg_min(TimeGenerated, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName) by Computer, NewProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
    | where Spawns >= 10
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName=NewProcessName, Detail=strcat("WorkerStorm spawns=", tostring(Spawns)), Platform="Windows";
union LinuxOOM, WinIISCrash, WinWorkerStorm
| summarize CrashEvents=count(), arg_min(TimeGenerated, ProcessName, Detail), arg_max(TimeGenerated, ProcessName) by Computer, Platform
| where CrashEvents >= 3
| order by CrashEvents desc
(source:linux.syslog @log.message:*oom-killer* @log.message:(*nginx* OR *httpd* OR *apache2* OR *envoy*)) OR (source:windows.security @EventID:1000 (@Image:(*\\w3wp.exe OR *\\W3WP.exe OR *\\nginx.exe OR *\\Nginx.exe OR *\\httpd.exe OR *\\Httpd.exe OR *\\envoy.exe OR *\\Envoy.exe))) OR (source:windows.security @EventID:4688 @NewProcessName:(*\\w3wp.exe OR *\\W3WP.exe OR *\\nginx.exe OR *\\Nginx.exe OR *\\httpd.exe OR *\\envoy.exe))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(nginx|httpd|w3wp|envoy|apache2)(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName], function=[count(as=spawns), min(_time, as=first_spawn), max(_time, as=last_spawn)])
| spawns >= 10
| storm_window_sec := last_spawn - first_spawn

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

Critical

Autonomous AI Tool Finds 2-Year-Old RCE Flaw in Redis (CVE-2026-23479)

The Hacker News
2026-06-03 8 use cases 5 techniques 4 kill-chain phases detected

Redis has patched a use-after-free in its blocking-client code that lets an authenticated user run arbitrary OS commands on the machine hosting the database. The flaw was found by an autonomous AI tool built to hunt bugs in large codebases. Tracked as CVE-2026-23479, the flaw was introduced in Redis 7.2.0 and remained in every stable branch until the May 5 fixes, unnoticed for over two years.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Vulnerable Redis versions exposed to CVE-2026-23479 (TVM inventory pivot) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Redis-server process spawning shell or scripting interpreter (CVE-2026-23479 RCE) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Redis-server process spawning shell or scripting interpreter (CVE-2026-23479 RCE) Exploitation High
Hunts the terminal stage of the CVE-2026-23479 exploit chain: the use-after-free in unblockClientOnKey() ultimately repoints strcasecmp() to system() via a GOT overwrite, so the next Redis command is executed as a shell command. Any child process of redis-server that is a shell, scripting interpreter, or download tool is a high-fidelity indicator of in-the-wild exploitation. Rationale: Article describes that the GOT overwrite repoints strcasecmp() to system(), so 'the next command Redis parses runs as a shell command.' That child shell will be parented to redis-server in EDR telemetry — an extremely rare event in any legitimate Redis deployment. No second source needed: the parent-child relationship is a direct consequence of the published exploit chain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/redis-cve-2026-23479-uaf • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-23479
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("redis-server","redis-server.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/redis-server"
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "\\redis-server.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wget","curl","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby","php")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
imProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "/redis-server" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\redis-server.exe" or ParentProcessName =~ "redis-server" or ParentProcessName =~ "redis-server.exe"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/zsh","/ksh","\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","/wget","/curl","/nc","/ncat","/socat","/python","/python3","/perl","/ruby","/php")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Vulnerable Redis versions exposed to CVE-2026-23479 (TVM inventory pivot) Reconnaissance High
Surfaces every managed host running a Redis version in the vulnerable range (7.2.0-7.2.13, 7.4.0-7.4.8, 8.2.0-8.2.5, 8.4.0-8.4.2, 8.6.0-8.6.2) so the SOC can drive emergency patching and tighten ACLs before the public exploit chain is weaponised. Vulnerability is authenticated-only but the article highlights that most cloud Redis deployments use the default user with all required ACL categories. Rationale: Article tables the exact vulnerable/fixed version ranges per branch. TVM-based hunting is the cleanest way to drive emergency patching before public PoC is weaponised; pivot via IsInternetFacing because the article highlights cloud-exposed Redis as the primary at-risk surface. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/redis/redis/security/advisories • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-23479
ATT&CKT1190 T1212
Data sourcesEndpoint.Vulnerabilities
let VulnerableRedis =
    DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
    | where SoftwareVendor =~ "redis" and SoftwareName has "redis"
    | extend Parts = split(SoftwareVersion, ".")
    | extend Major = toint(Parts[0]), Minor = toint(Parts[1]), Patch = toint(Parts[2])
    | where (Major == 7 and Minor == 2 and Patch <= 13)
         or (Major == 7 and Minor == 4 and Patch <= 8)
         or (Major == 8 and Minor == 2 and Patch <= 5)
         or (Major == 8 and Minor == 4 and Patch <= 2)
         or (Major == 8 and Minor == 6 and Patch <= 2);
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-23479"
| union VulnerableRedis
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
let VulnerableRedis =
    DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where CveId == "CVE-2026-23479" or (SoftwareVendor =~ "redis" and SoftwareName has "redis");
VulnerableRedis
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, CveId
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High

Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Google DoubleClick Abused in New Malspam Campaign to Deliver DesckVB RAT

The Hacker News
2026-06-03 16 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have flagged a new malspam campaign that makes use of Google's DoubleClick domain as a way to evade detection and ultimately deliver a remote access trojan (RAT) named DesckVB RAT. "Before the victim ever reaches attacker-controlled infrastructure, the lure routes through DoubleClick, a legitimate Google-owned domain that many security tools are less likely to treat as

Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] PowerShell fetching DesckVB .NET loader from pastee.dev · [LLM] DesckVB C2 raw TCP beacon to known infrastructure (IPs + DDNS + hostgator domain) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains

[LLM] HTML attachment with meta-refresh redirect via Google DoubleClick to malspam landing Delivery Medium
Hunts the DesckVB delivery vector: phishing email with an .html attachment that meta-refreshes the browser through a doubleclick.net click-tracking URL into an attacker-controlled redirector. Pivots EmailAttachmentInfo (.html) joined with UrlClickEvents to doubleclick.net within a small window. Rationale: Article explicitly states the HTML attachment 'triggers a meta-refresh browser redirect to a Google DoubleClick Campaign Manager click-tracking URL'. The HTML + doubleclick.net pivot within a tight time window is the distinguishing signal — generic doubleclick traffic from ad-loaded browsing isn't preceded by an email-attached HTML open. Cross-checked against: • https://www.huntress.com/blog/desckvb-rat-malspam
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.001 T1102
Data sourcesEmail.Email_Attachments Web.Web
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let HtmlAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName endswith ".html" or FileName endswith ".htm"
    | project EmailTime = Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress, FileName, SHA256;
let DoubleClickClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where Url has_any ("doubleclick.net", "ad.doubleclick.net", "googleadservices.com")
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed", "ClickedThrough");
HtmlAttachments
| join kind=inner DoubleClickClicks on $left.RecipientEmailAddress == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 30m)
| project EmailTime, ClickTime = Timestamp, RecipientEmailAddress, FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256, Url, NetworkMessageId
| order by EmailTime desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let PhishedRecipients = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where Operation has_any ("FileMalwareDetected", "AttachmentDetected")
    | distinct UserId;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where Url has_any ("doubleclick.net/click", "ad.doubleclick.net", "googleadservices.com/pagead")
| where SrcUsername in (PhishedRecipients) or HttpRequestHeaderReferer has_any (".html", ".htm")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpRequestHeaderReferer, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(windows.defender OR azure.activeDirectory) (@evt.name:EmailAttachmentInfo OR @evt.name:UrlClickEvents) (@FileName:(*.html OR *.htm) OR @Url:(*doubleclick.net* OR *ad.doubleclick.net*))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/doubleclick\.net|googleadservices\.com/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/outlook\.exe|chrome\.exe|msedge\.exe/i CommandLine=/\.html?/i}, field=aid)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName], function=count())
WEB

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Email where Email.file_name="*.html" OR Email.file_name="*.htm" by Email.src_user Email.recipient Email.message_id Email.file_name Email.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Email)` | join type=inner message_id [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*doubleclick.net*" OR Web.url="*ad.doubleclick.net*" by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.message_id | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | where lastTime - firstTime < 600
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Email where Email.file_name="*.html" OR Email.file_name="*.htm" by Email.src_user Email.recipient Email.message_id Email.file_name Email.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Email)` | join type=inner message_id [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*doubleclick.net*" OR Web.url="*ad.doubleclick.net*" by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.message_id | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | where lastTime - firstTime < 600
[LLM] ZIP-borne JavaScript loader spawning PowerShell from user Downloads Installation High
Hunts the second-stage DesckVB execution: ZIP archive downloaded from the malspam landing page contains a .js file that wscript.exe/cscript.exe runs, which then extracts and launches PowerShell to fetch the .NET loader. Detects the Downloads-folder JS → PowerShell parent-child chain. Rationale: Article: 'a JavaScript loader, whose main responsibility is to retrieve and execute a .NET RAT... The script extracts and runs a PowerShell script'. The Downloads/Temp parent-path constraint plus the wscript→powershell chain is the load-bearing combination from the article's ZIP-attached-from-landing-page narrative. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/007/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe", "cscript.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (".js", ".jse", ".vbs", ".wsf")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("explorer.exe", "7zG.exe", "WinRAR.exe", "7zFM.exe", "chrome.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          GrandparentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe", "cscript.exe")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (".js", ".jse", ".vbs", ".wsf")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ZIP-borne JS Loader Spawning PowerShell from Downloads (DesckVB)
id: 7d4e2c91-3a8f-4b62-9d1e-5f8a2c7b9d10
description: Detects wscript.exe or cscript.exe in the user Downloads/Temp path spawning PowerShell — the DesckVB RAT delivery chain seen in the Huntress June 2026 DoubleClick malspam campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-doubleclick-abused-in-new.html
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - '.js'
      - '.jse'
      - '.vbs'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
  selection_path:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Roaming\'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate enterprise scripts launched manually by power users
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\wscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\CScript.exe) @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe) @ParentCommandLine:(*.js* OR *.vbs*) @ParentCommandLine:(*\Downloads\* OR *\Temp\* OR *\AppData\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd)\.exe$/i
| regex("\\\\(Downloads|Temp|AppData\\\\(Local|Roaming))\\\\", field=ParentCommandLine)
| regex("\\.(js|jse|vbs|wsf)", field=ParentCommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentCommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") AND Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" AND (Processes.parent_process LIKE "%\\Downloads\\%" OR Processes.parent_process LIKE "%\\Temp\\%" OR Processes.parent_process LIKE "%.js%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
[LLM] PowerShell fetching DesckVB .NET loader from pastee.dev Command & Control High
Hunts the stager retrieval step: PowerShell making outbound HTTPS to pastee.dev (the article-named payload-hosting service) to download the .NET loader. The pastee.dev domain is specific to this campaign and not a common enterprise destination. Rationale: pastee.dev is explicitly listed as IOC infrastructure. PowerShell → pastee.dev outbound is rarely a legitimate enterprise pattern (paste-share sites aren't typical PowerShell module sources). Bound to specific named binary + named domain = high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-doubleclick-abused-in-new.html
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has "pastee.dev" or RemoteUrl endswith "pastee.dev"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DstHostname has "pastee.dev" or Url has "pastee.dev"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] DesckVB Defender exclusion configuration via Add-MpPreference / WMIC Installation High
Hunts DesckVB's tamper step where the loader 'configures Microsoft Defender exclusions' before dropping the RAT. Detects Add-MpPreference / Set-MpPreference with ExclusionPath/ExclusionProcess from non-admin process contexts spawned by the malspam chain. Rationale: Article: 'neutralizes the machine's security controls' and 'configures Microsoft Defender exclusions'. The Add-MpPreference + Exclusion* combination is the canonical realisation. Filtering on non-GPO parents removes the legitimate admin path and keeps the loader-driven path. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference", "Set-MpPreference")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("ExclusionPath", "ExclusionProcess", "ExclusionExtension", "DisableRealtimeMonitoring", "DisableIOAVProtection", "DisableBehaviorMonitoring")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("gpscript.exe", "SenseIR.exe", "MsSense.exe", "MpCmdRun.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          ProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference", "Set-MpPreference")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("ExclusionPath", "ExclusionProcess", "ExclusionExtension", "DisableRealtimeMonitoring", "DisableBehaviorMonitoring")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName !has_any ("gpscript.exe", "MsSense.exe", "MpCmdRun.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Defender Exclusion Added by Non-Admin Tooling (DesckVB Tamper)
id: 9b3c4d8e-2f5a-4e71-b8c2-7d4e9f1a6b35
description: Detects Add-MpPreference / Set-MpPreference with ExclusionPath/ExclusionProcess/DisableRealtimeMonitoring, scoped to non-GPO parents — matches DesckVB loader behaviour described in Huntress June 2026 report.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-doubleclick-abused-in-new.html
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_exec:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Add-MpPreference'
      - 'Set-MpPreference'
  selection_args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'ExclusionPath'
      - 'ExclusionProcess'
      - 'ExclusionExtension'
      - 'DisableRealtimeMonitoring'
      - 'DisableBehaviorMonitoring'
  filter_legit:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\gpscript.exe'
      - '\MsSense.exe'
      - '\MpCmdRun.exe'
  condition: selection_exec and selection_cmd and selection_args and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Sysadmins manually adding exclusions during AV exception requests
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe) (@CommandLine:*Add-MpPreference* OR @CommandLine:*Set-MpPreference*) (@CommandLine:*ExclusionPath* OR @CommandLine:*ExclusionProcess* OR @CommandLine:*DisableRealtimeMonitoring*) -@ParentImage:(*\gpscript.exe OR *\MsSense.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd)\.exe$/i
| regex("(Add|Set)-MpPreference", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(ExclusionPath|ExclusionProcess|ExclusionExtension|DisableRealtimeMonitoring|DisableBehaviorMonitoring)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/^(gpscript|MsSense|MpCmdRun)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%Add-MpPreference%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%Set-MpPreference%") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%ExclusionPath%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%ExclusionProcess%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%ExclusionExtension%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%DisableRealtimeMonitoring%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
[LLM] DesckVB persistence via Run/RunOnce + Startup folder loader drop Installation Medium
Hunts the DesckVB persistence step: registry Run/RunOnce write OR a binary placed in the user Startup folder by a process descended from the PowerShell loader chain. The article calls out both vectors as part of the same install step. Rationale: Article: 'persistence is established on the host by setting up Run and RunOnce Registry entries, along with placing a loader responsible for launching the RAT in the user's Startup folder'. The dual-path detection covers both vectors as one logical unit. Constrains to script-host parents to avoid noisy installer hits. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/
ATT&CKT1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Filesystem
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RunKeys = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet", "RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
    | where RegistryValueData has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Public\")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "cmd.exe", "regsvr32.exe", "rundll32.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, 
              Vector = "RunKey", 
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              Image = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              ImageCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              KeyPath = RegistryKey,
              ValueName = RegistryValueName,
              ValueData = RegistryValueData;
let StartupDrops = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed")
    | where FolderPath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "cmd.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              Vector = "StartupFolder",
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              Image = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              ImageCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              KeyPath = FolderPath,
              ValueName = FileName,
              ValueData = SHA256;
RunKeys
| union StartupDrops
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RunKeys = ImRegistryEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
    | where RegistryValueData has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Public\")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "cmd.exe")
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Vector = "RunKey",
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData;
let StartupDrops = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where TargetFilePath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "cmd.exe")
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Vector = "StartupFolder",
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              RegistryKey = TargetFilePath, RegistryValue = TargetFileName, RegistryValueData = TargetFileSHA256;
RunKeys
| union StartupDrops
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\CurrentVersion\Run\* OR *\CurrentVersion\RunOnce\*) @Details:(*\AppData\* OR *\ProgramData\* OR *\Temp\*) @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\Start*Menu\Programs\Startup\* OR *\Start*Menu\Programs\StartUp\*) @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe))
(#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate RegObjectName=/\\CurrentVersion\\Run(Once)?$/i RegStringValue=/\\(AppData|ProgramData|Temp|Public)\\/i ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|cmd)\.exe$/i)
OR (#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\Start Menu\\Programs\\Startup\\/i ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|cmd)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RegObjectName, RegStringValue, TargetFileName], function=count())

[LLM] DesckVB C2 raw TCP beacon to known infrastructure (IPs + DDNS + hostgator domain) Command & Control High
Hunts the DesckVB RAT's command-and-control channel: raw TCP outbound to article-published infrastructure — 23.186.113.60, 45.156.87.226, manikandan83.mysynology.net (DDNS), or the long meusitehostgator.com.br subdomain. Triggers on any internal host reaching any of these endpoints from any process. Rationale: Direct IOC hit list from the article's pre-extracted IOCs. The mysynology.net DDNS + the unusually long 1552093.meusitehostgator.com.br subdomain are both campaign-specific. Even one DNS query to these names from an internal host is alert-worthy. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-doubleclick-abused-in-new.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1095
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let DesckVBIPs = dynamic(["23.186.113.60", "45.156.87.226"]);
let DesckVBDomains = dynamic(["manikandan83.mysynology.net", "andrefelipedonascime1768785037020.1552093.meusitehostgator.com.br", "pastee.dev"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (DesckVBIPs)
    or RemoteUrl has_any (DesckVBDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let DesckVBIPs = dynamic(["23.186.113.60", "45.156.87.226"]);
let DesckVBDomains = dynamic(["manikandan83.mysynology.net", "andrefelipedonascime1768785037020.1552093.meusitehostgator.com.br", "pastee.dev"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in (DesckVBIPs)
    or DstHostname in~ (DesckVBDomains)
    or Url has_any (DesckVBDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername,
          DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol,
          NetworkBytes, NetworkDuration, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
