Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-48595")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"

| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 path traversal — file written from WinRAR into Startup folder · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] GammaPhish HTA auto-execution — mshta.exe launching from user Startup folder · [LLM] GammaWorm NTFS Alternate Data Stream module hide — script-host writes file with ADS suffix · [LLM] GammaSteel registry-staged module fan-out — PowerShell writes many binary blobs under one key · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GammaWorm Telegram/Telegraph/Teletype/Cloudflare-Workers DDR resolution via curl from script host · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] GammaWorm USB / network-share propagation — script process mass-creates LNK files on removable or remote drives · [LLM] GammaSteel S3 exfiltration — script/PowerShell HTTP egress to AWS S3 bucket · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 path traversal — file written from WinRAR into Startup folder Delivery High
Hunts the GammaPhish initial-access signature: a WinRAR / UnRAR / RAR process writes a file into a Windows Startup directory. CVE-2025-8088 lets a malicious archive traverse out of the chosen extraction path; Gamaredon weaponises it to drop an HTA dropper that auto-runs at next logon. Rationale: Article + Sekoia explicitly state the WinRAR exploit drops an HTA into the Startup directory via path traversal. Pairing the archive-tool image with the Startup destination is the cleanest single-event signature for CVE-2025-8088 exploitation. Cross-checked Sekoia blog and follow-on Hacker News CVE-2025-8088 coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/fsbs-matryoshka-1-3-gamaredons-gifts-that-keeps-unpacking-gammaphish-and-gammaworm/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/01/google-warns-of-active-exploitation-of.html • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/gamaredon-worm-ntfs-data-streams/
ATT&CKT1203 T1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(7d) | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winrar.exe","unrar.exe","rar.exe") | where FolderPath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\" | where FileName !endswith ".log" and FileName !endswith ".tmp" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, ArchiveTool=InitiatingProcessFileName, ArchiveCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, DroppedFile=FileName, DropPath=FolderPath, SHA256 | order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where ActingProcessName has_any ("winrar.exe","unrar.exe","rar.exe") | where TargetFilePath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256 | order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GammaPhish HTA auto-execution — mshta.exe launching from user Startup folder Installation High
Hunts the GammaPhish auto-run: at next logon, explorer.exe launches mshta.exe against an HTA that CVE-2025-8088 dropped into the Startup folder. Pairing the parent (explorer) with the binary (mshta) and the HTA's path (Startup) is a high-fidelity catch for the post-exploit handoff to GammaLoad. Rationale: Sekoia and Hacker News articles describe the GammaPhish HTA being dropped directly into the Startup folder by the WinRAR exploit, which then auto-launches via mshta at logon. Combining explorer→mshta parentage with the Startup path eliminates the bulk of mshta noise from legitimate HTAs hosted elsewhere. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/fsbs-matryoshka-1-3-gamaredons-gifts-that-keeps-unpacking-gammaphish-and-gammaworm/ • https://cyberpress.org/gamaredon-apt-hides-malware/

SecurityEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where EventID == 4688 | where NewProcessName endswith "\\mshta.exe" | where ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe" | where CommandLine has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\" | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine | order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GammaWorm Telegram/Telegraph/Teletype/Cloudflare-Workers DDR resolution via curl from script host Command & Control High
Hunts the GammaWorm dead-drop-resolver step: a VBScript host (wscript / cscript / mshta) spawns curl.exe to fetch a hardcoded public Telegram channel page (t.me/telegra.ph) or its Teletype.in / Cloudflare Workers fall-back, from which the actual C2 address is parsed. Catches the exact platform abuse Sekoia documents. Rationale: Sekoia's report explicitly names Telegram, Telegra.ph, Teletype.in, and Cloudflare Workers as Gamaredon's DDR platforms, and curl as the GammaWorm fetch tool. Pairing curl with a script-host parent and one of these four domains is single-event-shape and very rare in a legit corporate environment. One of the article IOCs (bold.zsjtn41091.workers.dev) is a Cloudflare Workers DDR endpoint. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/fsbs-matryoshka-1-3-gamaredons-gifts-that-keeps-unpacking-gammaphish-and-gammaworm/ • https://cyberpress.org/gamaredon-apt-hides-malware/
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1071.001 T1059.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(7d) | where FileName =~ "curl.exe" | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe") | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("t.me/","telegra.ph","teletype.in",".workers.dev") | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ScriptHost=InitiatingProcessFileName, ScriptCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, CurlCmd=ProcessCommandLine | order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where ActingProcessName endswith "curl.exe" | where ParentProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe") | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("t.me/","telegra.ph","teletype.in",".workers.dev") | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine | order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GammaWorm USB / network-share propagation — script process mass-creates LNK files on removable or remote drives Actions on Objectives High
Hunts GammaWorm's lateral-movement pattern: a VBScript host (wscript / cscript) writes many .lnk files to a removable drive or network share within a short window, while concurrently setting the hidden attribute on existing directories. The shortcut-replacing technique is Gamaredon's documented spread vector for USB and SMB. Rationale: Article specifies GammaWorm 'hide legitimate directories in network shares and USB drives and replace with malicious Windows Shortcut (LNK) files.' Detection keys on script-host parentage + drive letter outside C: or UNC root + LNK extension + burst count — none of these alone are unusual, but the combination is. Skipped Sigma because the threshold/grouping is multi-event correlation. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/fsbs-matryoshka-1-3-gamaredons-gifts-that-keeps-unpacking-gammaphish-and-gammaworm/ • https://cyberpress.org/gamaredon-apt-hides-malware/
ATT&CKT1091 T1080 T1547.009
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(7d) | where ActionType == "FileCreated" | where FileName endswith ".lnk" | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") | where FolderPath matches regex @"^(\\\\[^\\]+\\|[D-Z]:\\)" | summarize LnkCount=dcount(FileName), Samples=make_set(FileName, 5), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 10m) | where LnkCount >= 5
ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where EventType == "FileCreated" | where TargetFileName endswith ".lnk" | where ActingProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") | where TargetFilePath matches regex @"^(\\\\[^\\]+\\|[D-Z]:\\)" | summarize LnkCount=dcount(TargetFileName), Samples=make_set(TargetFileName, 5) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m) | where LnkCount >= 5
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@Image:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe)) (@TargetFilename:(*.lnk OR *.LNK)) (@TargetFilename:(\\\\* OR D\:\\* OR E\:\\* OR F\:\\* OR G\:\\*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i TargetFileName=/\.lnk$/i | regex("^(\\\\\\\\|[D-Z]:\\\\)", field=TargetFileName) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function={lnk_count := count(TargetFileName, distinct=true) | first := min(_time)}) | lnk_count >= 5
ENDPOINT

[LLM] GammaWorm NTFS Alternate Data Stream module hide — script-host writes file with ADS suffix Installation Medium
Hunts the GammaWorm defence-evasion technique: a VBScript host writes one of its core modules into an Alternate Data Stream (filename:streamname pattern) on a host file. Sekoia documents this as the primary on-disk hiding mechanism for the worm's modules. Rationale: Article + Infosecurity Magazine + Sekoia all confirm GammaWorm uses NTFS Alternate Data Streams to conceal its core modules. Script-host parentage + ADS-shape filename + Zone.Identifier exclusion is the cleanest single-event match. Cross-checked Infosecurity Magazine for technique confirmation. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/fsbs-matryoshka-1-3-gamaredons-gifts-that-keeps-unpacking-gammaphish-and-gammaworm/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/gamaredon-worm-ntfs-data-streams/ • https://undercodenews.com/silent-infiltration-russian-linked-gamaredon-worm-exploits-windows-hidden-streams-to-haunt-ukrainian-systems-without-a-trace-video/
ATT&CKT1564.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(7d) | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") | where FileName matches regex @"^[^:]+:[^:\\/]+$" | where FileName !endswith ":Zone.Identifier" and FileName !endswith ":SmartScreen" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, ScriptHost=InitiatingProcessFileName, ScriptCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ADSFile=FileName, ADSPath=FolderPath | order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where ActingProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") | where TargetFileName matches regex @"^[^:]+:[^:\\/]+$" | where TargetFileName !endswith ":Zone.Identifier" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath | order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GammaSteel registry-staged module fan-out — PowerShell writes many binary blobs under one key Installation Medium
Hunts GammaSteel's documented self-staging behaviour: the PowerShell-based stealer writes ~71 DPAPI-encrypted modules as binary values into a single registry key, used as its in-memory loading store. The fan-out of binary registry values from a single PowerShell process to one parent key is article-specific and very rare. Rationale: Sekoia and follow-on coverage describe GammaSteel staging 71 encrypted PowerShell modules in the registry, protected by Windows DPAPI. Threshold ≥20 distinct binary values under one HKCU/HKLM\Software key written by a single PowerShell/wscript process in 30 minutes catches the staging without over-firing on legitimate per-value config writes. Multi-event correlation, so Sigma is intentionally skipped. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/fsbs-matryoshka-1-3-gamaredons-gifts-that-keeps-unpacking-gammaphish-and-gammaworm/ • https://cyberpress.org/gamaredon-apt-hides-malware/

[LLM] GammaSteel S3 exfiltration — script/PowerShell HTTP egress to AWS S3 bucket Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the GammaSteel exfiltration path: a script host or PowerShell process not normally seen on the wire issues an outbound HTTPS connection to *.s3.amazonaws.com (or s3.<region>.amazonaws.com) to upload harvested files. Article specifies S3 as the primary exfil with attacker-controlled web servers as a fallback. Rationale: Article explicitly names AWS S3 as GammaSteel's exfil destination with attacker-controlled fallback. The hunt isolates the unusual combination of script-host parentage and S3 egress — neither AWSPowerShell nor aws-cli are in the included process list, so legitimate S3 backup activity from a developer workstation falls outside scope. Tier set to hunting because S3 is widely used; analyst should pivot from any hit to the parent process chain. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sekoia.io/fsbs-matryoshka-1-3-gamaredons-gifts-that-keeps-unpacking-gammaphish-and-gammaworm/ • https://cyberpress.org/gamaredon-apt-hides-malware/

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")

        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

     | rename Processes.user as user]

union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — The npm Threat Landscape: Attack Surface and Mitigations (Updated June 2)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm/node lifecycle script fetching Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun · [LLM] Malicious @bitwarden/cli payload artifacts on disk (bw_setup.js, bw1.js, Shai-Hulud markers)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 beacon to audit.checkmarx[.]cx /v1/telemetry (TeamPCP Shai-Hulud Third Coming) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] npm/node lifecycle script fetching Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun Installation High
Detects an npm preinstall/postinstall lifecycle script (node.exe parented by npm) reaching out to github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases to download the Bun v1.3.13 runtime. This is the exact bootstrap behaviour of the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 payload (bw_setup.js Stage-1) and is highly anomalous on developer endpoints because legitimate JS projects rarely pull Bun via a package-install hook. Rationale: Article explicitly names github.com/oven-sh/bun and Bun v1.3.13 as the runtime downloaded by Stage-1 bw_setup.js during npm preinstall — pairing the github.com/oven-sh/bun URL token with an npm-family parent process is a near-zero-FP signature on production endpoints (developer laptops will produce occasional FPs, hence the parent-process pinning). Cross-checked against Socket and Checkmarx advisories listed below. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain • https://checkmarx.com/blog/checkmarx-supply-chain-incident-april-2026/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let bunUrlIndicators = dynamic(["github.com/oven-sh/bun", "oven-sh/bun/releases", "bun-windows-x64", "bun-linux-x64", "bun-darwin"]);
let npmParents = dynamic(["npm.exe","npm-cli.js","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe"]);
let downloaderChildren = dynamic(["node.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","pwsh.exe"]);
// Process-tree pivot — npm parent spawning a downloader child with Bun URL on the command line
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (npmParents) or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (npmParents)
    | where FileName in~ (downloaderChildren)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              InitImage  = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitCmd    = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildImage = FileName,
              ChildCmd   = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
// Network pivot — same process families connecting to github.com for the Bun release tarball
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where RemoteUrl has "github.com" and (RemoteUrl has "oven-sh/bun" or RemoteUrl has "bun-windows" or RemoteUrl has "bun-linux" or RemoteUrl has "bun-darwin")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (downloaderChildren)
    | where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (npmParents) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              InitImage   = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitCmd     = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildImage  = "<network-egress>", ChildCmd = RemoteUrl, SHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256;
union ProcHits, NetHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let bunUrlIndicators = dynamic(["github.com/oven-sh/bun", "oven-sh/bun/releases", "bun-windows-x64", "bun-linux-x64", "bun-darwin"]);
let npmParents = dynamic(["npm.exe","npm-cli.js","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe","npm","node","yarn","pnpm","npx"]);
let downloaderChildren = dynamic(["node.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","pwsh.exe","node","curl","wget","bun","bash","sh","pwsh"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any (downloaderChildren) or ParentProcessName has_any (downloaderChildren)
| where (ParentProcessName has_any (npmParents) or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents))
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators) or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"

title: NPM Lifecycle Script Downloading Bun Runtime from oven-sh GitHub
id: 4c2f6f8a-9d1e-4b8c-9a3f-2e8a0b1c4d51
status: experimental
description: Detects an npm/yarn/pnpm install lifecycle script (Node.js parented by npm) spawning a downloader to fetch the Bun JavaScript runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun — the Stage-1 bootstrap of the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli supply-chain payload.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/monitoring-npm-supply-chain-attacks/
  - https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'

falsepositives:

  - CI agent installing Bun in a build pipeline (scope detection to dev workstations or scope out CI hosts)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\npm.exe OR *\NPM.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\NODE.exe OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe OR *\npx.exe) @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\CURL.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\bun.exe) @CommandLine:(*github.com/oven-sh/bun* OR *oven-sh/bun/releases* OR *bun-windows-x64* OR *bun-linux-x64* OR *bun-darwin*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|node|yarn|pnpm|npx)(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(node|curl|powershell|pwsh|wget|bun|bash|sh)\.exe$/i
| regex("github\.com/oven-sh/bun|oven-sh/bun/releases|bun-(windows|linux|darwin)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] C2 beacon to audit.checkmarx[.]cx /v1/telemetry (TeamPCP Shai-Hulud Third Coming) Command & Control High
Detects any outbound network/DNS activity to the TeamPCP C2 audit.checkmarx[.]cx (94.154.172.43) — particularly POSTs to the /v1/telemetry path — that exfiltrates harvested cloud, CI/CD and developer credentials from compromised hosts. The domain visually impersonates Checkmarx's legitimate infrastructure but resolves to attacker-controlled space. Rationale: Article Table 1 names the C2 server, IP and HTTP path explicitly (audit.checkmarx[.]cx:443 / 94.154.172.43 / /v1/telemetry) — any hit on these three indicators is a confirmed-compromise signal, not a hunting hypothesis. Corroborated by Checkmarx's official disclosure that all four artifact families (npm, Docker Hub, GitHub Actions, VS Code) shared this C2. Cross-checked against: • https://checkmarx.com/blog/checkmarx-supply-chain-incident-april-2026/ • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let c2Hosts = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx", "audit.checkmarx[.]cx"]);
let c2Ips    = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let c2Path   = "/v1/telemetry";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (RemoteUrl has_any (c2Hosts)) or (RemoteIP in (c2Ips)) or (RemoteUrl has c2Path and RemotePort in (443, 80))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","SenseIR.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2Hosts = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);
let c2Ips    = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let c2Path   = "/v1/telemetry";
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstHostname has_any (c2Hosts) or DstIpAddr in (c2Ips) or (isnotempty(Url) and Url has c2Path and DstPortNumber in (443, 80))
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkApplicationProtocol
),
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (c2Hosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsQueryTypeName, DnsResponseCodeName
),
(
  ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where HttpHostName has_any (c2Hosts) or Url has c2Path and (HttpHostName has "checkmarx.cx")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, HttpHostName, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (c2Hosts) or DestinationIP in (c2Ips) or RequestURL has "audit.checkmarx.cx" or RequestURL has c2Path
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP Shai-Hulud C2 audit.checkmarx[.]cx Connection
id: 7e5a3b2c-1f4d-4a6e-9b8f-3c2d1e4f5a62
status: experimental
description: Detects connections or DNS resolutions to the TeamPCP / Shai-Hulud Third Coming C2 infrastructure (audit.checkmarx[.]cx / 94.154.172.43) used by the @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 npm supply-chain payload and the broader Checkmarx-distribution-channel compromise to exfiltrate harvested credentials via /v1/telemetry.

[LLM] Malicious @bitwarden/cli payload artifacts on disk (bw_setup.js, bw1.js, Shai-Hulud markers) Installation High
Detects creation or execution of the Stage-1 (bw_setup.js) and Stage-2 (bw1.js) Node.js scripts dropped by the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 npm package, as well as the 'Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming' string written into public repo content that the worm uses as an attribution marker and propagation beacon. This catches both the install-time drop on the npm install path and any post-compromise replay. Rationale: Article explicitly names bw_setup.js (Stage-1 bootstrap, registered as the `bw` bin) and bw1.js (Stage-2 Bun payload) inside the malicious @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 package. The legitimate Bitwarden CLI ships neither filename, so the filename + package path combo is a hard-IOC match. The Shai-Hulud Third Coming string is a TeamPCP attribution marker per the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain • https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/security/advisories
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let stageFiles = dynamic(["bw_setup.js", "bw1.js"]);
let packageHints = dynamic(["@bitwarden\\cli", "@bitwarden/cli", "node_modules\\@bitwarden\\cli", "node_modules/@bitwarden/cli"]);
let shaiHuludMarker = "Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where (FileName in~ (stageFiles)) or (FolderPath has_any (packageHints) and FileName endswith ".js") or (AdditionalFields has shaiHuludMarker)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              FolderPath, FileName, SHA256;
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (stageFiles)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              FolderPath, FileName = FileName, SHA256, ProcCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let stageFiles = dynamic(["bw_setup.js", "bw1.js"]);
let packageHints = dynamic(["@bitwarden\\cli", "@bitwarden/cli", "node_modules\\@bitwarden\\cli", "node_modules/@bitwarden/cli"]);
let npmRunners = dynamic(["npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe","npm","node","yarn","pnpm","bun"]);
let FileHits = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where (TargetFileName in~ (stageFiles)) or (TargetFilePath has_any (packageHints) and TargetFileExtension =~ "js")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256;
let ProcHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (npmRunners) or ParentProcessName has_any (npmRunners)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (stageFiles)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              TargetFilePath = "", TargetFileName = "", TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256;
union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

High

Multiple redhat-cloud-services npm Packages compromised

StepSecurity
2026-06-02 10 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Several packages in the @redhat-cloud-services npm scope were found to carry malicious payloads that fire via a preinstall hook on every npm install. The affected versions span multiple packages across the RedHat Cloud Services frontend ecosystem. The payload is a sophisticated multi-stage credential harvester that targets GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, and CircleCI tokens

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Bun runtime download to /tmp from a node process during npm install · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Multiple redhat-cloud-services npm Packages compromised
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm preinstall hook executing oversized node index.js from @redhat-cloud-services package · [LLM] Bun spawned from npm install context executing /tmp/p*.js implant
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Process reading /proc/<pid>/mem of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker (in-memory secret extraction)
[LLM] npm preinstall hook executing oversized node index.js from @redhat-cloud-services package Installation High
Detects the entry point of the @redhat-cloud-services supply-chain compromise: a preinstall script firing node against an unusually large (>1 MB) index.js shipped inside an @redhat-cloud-services scoped package directory. The legitimate libraries in this scope have tiny entry files, so a 4.2 MB index.js executing during install is a near-deterministic signal of the malicious version. Rationale: Anchors on the exact preinstall execution string named in package.json (`node index.js`) combined with the scoped-package path `@redhat-cloud-services` and the article's distinguishing 4.2 MB size of index.js (vs <100 KB for legitimate releases). Cross-checked against the StepSecurity disclosure and the three RedHatInsights GitHub issues (#492, #2329, #57). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/javascript-clients/issues/492 • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/frontend-components/issues/2329 • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/platform-frontend-ai-toolkit/issues/57
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007

[LLM] Bun runtime download to /tmp from a node process during npm install Delivery High
Detects Stage 3 of the redhat-cloud-services compromise: the in-memory _b downloader retrieves bun-v1.3.13 from the official Bun GitHub releases CDN and drops it into a randomly-named /tmp/ subdirectory, then registers it via globalThis.getBunPath. Article-specific because legitimate library installs never fetch a parallel JS runtime at install time. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact runtime version `bun-v1.3.13`, the GitHub releases CDN host (`objects.githubusercontent.com` is the actual blob host behind github.com release downloads), and the `/tmp/<random>/bun` drop path described in Stage 3. Pairs network event with the file-create within 5 minutes to suppress generic Bun installs on developer machines. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.3.13
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Filesystem
let BunDownload = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","npm")
    | where (RemoteUrl has "github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases" or RemoteUrl has "bun-v1.3.13" or RemoteUrl has "objects.githubusercontent.com")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP;
let BunDrop = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" or FolderPath startswith "/var/folders/"
    | where FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","tar","unzip")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
BunDownload
| join kind=inner BunDrop on DeviceId
| where Timestamp1 between (Timestamp .. Timestamp + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, DropPath = strcat(FolderPath, FileName), InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let BunNet = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where (Url has "github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases" or Url has "bun-v1.3.13" or DstHostname has "objects.githubusercontent.com")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm")
    | project NetTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Url, DstIpAddr;
let BunDrop = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated"
    | where TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/var/folders/"
    | where TargetFileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
    | project DropTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName;
BunNet
| join kind=inner BunDrop on DvcHostname
| where DropTime between (NetTime .. NetTime + 5m)
| project NetTime, DropTime, DvcHostname, Url, DstIpAddr, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by NetTime desc

[LLM] Process reading /proc/<pid>/mem of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker (in-memory secret extraction) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the credential-harvesting core of the implant: reading /proc/<pid>/mem of the GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process to scrape secrets that the runner holds in memory but never writes to disk. This is exactly the activity the StepSecurity Harden-Runner screenshot in the article captured and is the technique the payload uses to evade Harden-Runner-style detections by reading rather than calling out. Rationale: Anchors on /proc/<pid>/mem — the exact /proc read the article's Harden-Runner process-events screenshot captures — combined with node/bun as the reader (the Stage 1 entry point and the Stage 3 downloaded runtime). Joins forward to DeviceProcessEvents on the target PID to confirm it is Runner.Worker, eliminating debugger / strace noise. Source: StepSecurity blog + image SCR-20260601-oxms.png in-article screenshot showing Runner.Worker /proc/mem read. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/007/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/multiple-redhat-cloud-services-npm-packages-compromised
ATT&CKT1003.007 T1552.001 T1212
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileAccessed","FileCreated")
| where FolderPath startswith "/proc/" and FileName == "mem"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun")
| extend TargetPid = extract(@"/proc/(\d+)/", 1, FolderPath)
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName has_any ("Runner.Worker","Runner.Listener")
    | project DeviceId, TargetPid = tostring(ProcessId), RunnerCmd = ProcessCommandLine, RunnerName = FileName
) on DeviceId, TargetPid
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, TargetPid, RunnerName, RunnerCmd
| order by Timestamp desc
let ProcMemRe = @"/proc/\d+/mem";
let RunnerHits = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where SyslogMessage matches regex ProcMemRe
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("node", "bun")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
let AsimHits = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where TargetFilePath matches regex ProcMemRe
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node", "bun")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath;
union isfuzzy=true RunnerHits, AsimHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Bun spawned from npm install context executing /tmp/p*.js implant Installation High
Detects Stage 3→4 handoff: the freshly downloaded /tmp/<random>/bun binary executes a randomly-named /tmp/p<random>.js file containing the AES-decrypted main payload. Combination of Bun residing in /tmp/, being invoked by a node process whose CWD is inside an npm install, and immediately running a /tmp/p*.js is article-specific and effectively never benign. Rationale: Anchors on three article-specific shapes that compose into a near-zero-FP signal: Bun binary path under /tmp/<random>/bun (Stage 3 drop), parent in (node, npm, bun) (Stage 1 / Stage 3 chain), child commandline matching /tmp/p<random>.js (Stage 4 implant file). Each alone is noisy; together they reproduce the Stage 3→4 handoff in the StepSecurity write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/multiple-redhat-cloud-services-npm-packages-compromised • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1140/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1140 T1620
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" and FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/tmp/" and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","npm","bun")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/p[A-Za-z0-9]+\.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TmpJsRe = @"/tmp/p[A-Za-z0-9]+\.js";
let AsimHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where (ActingProcessName endswith "/bun" or ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or ActingProcessName endswith "/npm")
    | where TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex TmpJsRe or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex TmpJsRe
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine;
let SyslogHits = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where SyslogMessage matches regex TmpJsRe
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("bun", "node")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
union isfuzzy=true AsimHits, SyslogHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
