Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/

    category: process_creation

detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:

            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'

        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'

Laravel-Lang Supply Chain Attack: Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten to Steal CI Secrets

StepSecurity
2026-06-02 9 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

On May 22, 2026, an attacker with push access to the Laravel-Lang GitHub organization rewrote every git tag across multiple popular Composer packages within a single 15 minute window. Anyone running composer update or installing fresh against laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/actions, or laravel-lang/attributes now pulls a payload that exfiltrates CI secrets to a typosquatted attacker domain. StepSecurity confirmed end to end exploitation in an isolated runner and has filed security issues in all four repositories.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] GitHub bulk git tag force-push by single actor across multiple org repos
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PHP CLI drops hidden /tmp dropper artefacts (Laravel-Lang autoload payload) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Laravel-Lang Supply Chain Attack: Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Re

[LLM] Egress to typosquatted C2 flipboxstudio.info (Laravel-Lang Composer SC) Command & Control High
Hunts DNS or HTTP(S) callbacks to flipboxstudio.info, the attacker-controlled typosquat of the legitimate flipboxstudio.com used as the stage-1 fetch endpoint (/payload) and stage-2 exfiltration sink (/exfil) by the May 2026 Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain dropper. Single-IOC alerter — exact-domain match, near-zero FP expectation. Rationale: Anchors on the exact attacker-controlled domain `flipboxstudio.info` named verbatim in the IOC block as both the stage-1 GET endpoint (/payload) and stage-2 POST exfil endpoint (/exfil). The domain is a brand-new typosquat of flipboxstudio.com with no legitimate business use — any hit is high-fidelity.

[LLM] PHP CLI drops hidden /tmp dropper artefacts (Laravel-Lang autoload payload) Installation High
Hunts PHP CLI processes (typically from a composer-driven vendor/autoload.php boot) creating files under /tmp/.laravel_locale/<12-hex>.php or /tmp/.<8-hex> matching the exact dropper naming scheme generated by bin2hex(random_bytes(6)) in the malicious src/helpers.php. Combines hidden-path masquerade with the specific php-as-parent shape. Rationale: Anchors on the exact `/tmp/.laravel_locale/<12 hex chars>.php` PHP loader path and `/tmp/.<8 hex chars>` ELF path named in the IOC block, combined with the php-CLI parent shape that follows from `vendor/autoload.php` invoking the malicious helpers.php. The hex-length pattern matches the article's explicit `bin2hex(random_bytes(6))` naming generator.

[LLM] Orphaned process (ppid=1) executing from /tmp hidden hex path (post-dropper stage-2) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts processes reparented to init/systemd (ppid=1) whose image or command-line resolves to /tmp/.<6-12 hex chars> — the exact reparenting + execute-from-deleted-path shape left behind by the Laravel-Lang stage-2 loader after it backgrounds via `php "$f" > /dev/null 2>&1 &` and rm-deletes its own dropper files. Visible in process telemetry even after the file is unlinked. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit process IOCs: 'an orphaned php process with ppid=1' and 'an orphaned unnamed ELF process with ppid=1, executing from a now deleted path under /tmp'. Combines the reparent-to-init shape with the /tmp/.<hex> path generated by bin2hex(random_bytes(6)). Survives the self-delete because process metadata is captured at exec time.
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1564.001 T1070.004 T1620
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("systemd","init")
| where (FolderPath matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
   or (FileName matches regex @"^php[0-9]?$" and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}(\.php)?")
   or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("systemd","init") or ParentProcessId == 1
| where (ActingProcessName matches regex @"^/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}$")
   or (ActingProcessName endswith "/php" and ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/\.[a-f0-9]{6,12}(\.php)?")
   or (ActingProcessName startswith "/tmp/.laravel_locale")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessId, ActingProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GitHub bulk git tag force-push by single actor across multiple org repos Delivery Medium
Hunts the org-wide tag-rewrite shape that defined the initial-access step: one GitHub actor force-pushing tags across multiple repositories in the same org within a short window (the Laravel-Lang attacker rewrote 502+ tags across four repos in 88 minutes). Combine with commit-author imposter signature 'Your Name' / 'you@example.com'. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact shape: 'every git tag across multiple popular Composer packages within a single 15 minute window', 502 tags rewritten in one repo, four repos hit in 88 minutes, all by the same compromised credential. The commit-author imposter strings 'Your Name' / 'you@example.com' are also called out verbatim. Sentinel/Defender/Falcon are left empty because GitHub audit telemetry is not in their canonical schemas — Splunk and Datadog (via the GitHub integration) are the realistic shipping paths.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1078 T1098
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
source:github (@action:git.push OR @action:git.create) @git.ref:refs/tags/*
CLOUD
index=* sourcetype IN ("github:audit","github_audit_log","github:enterprise:audit") (action="git.push" OR action="git.create" OR action="protected_branch.policy_override") ref="refs/tags/*"
| eval repo_org=mvindex(split(repo,"/"),0)
| stats min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen dc(repo) as repo_count dc(ref) as tag_count values(repo) as repos values(ref) as refs by actor, repo_org
| eval window_seconds = last_seen - first_seen
| where tag_count >= 10 AND repo_count >= 2 AND window_seconds <= 3600
| eval window_minutes = round(window_seconds/60, 1)
| convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen)
| sort - tag_count

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)

| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port

| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort

| order by conn_count desc

            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Nx Console v18.95.0 Compromised VSIX / main.js / payload SHA-256 Hash Match · [LLM] macOS LaunchAgent Persistence — com.user.kitty-monitor.plist (Nx Console Compromise) · [LLM] Kitty cat.py Python Backdoor File Drop / Execution (Nx Console Compromise) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AWS IMDS (169.254.169.254) Hit from Developer / Non-EC2 Endpoint (Nx Console Credential Theft)
[LLM] Nx Console v18.95.0 Malicious Payload Bootstrap via Orphan Commit (npx github:nrwl/nx#558b09d7) Delivery High
Detects the malicious Nx Console v18.95.0 workspace-activation bootstrap step — npx (or node) executing code fetched from the dangling orphan commit 558b09d7 on github.com/nrwl/nx, spawned by a VS Code-family editor (Code, Code-Insiders, Cursor, Codium). This is the exact in-the-wild payload-fetch string published by StepSecurity. Rationale: The orphan-commit ref `558b09d7` (full SHA 558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2) and the `nrwl/nx#558b09d7` npx fragment are unique strings published in the StepSecurity report and confirmed by The Hacker News, GBHackers, and Cyberpress — no legitimate Nx workflow targets this hash. Parent constraint on VS Code-family editors anchors the workspace-activation behaviour described in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/ • https://cyberpress.org/nx-console-hijacked-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","code - insiders.exe","cursor.exe","codium.exe","vscodium.exe","electron","code helper","code","cursor","codium")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("github:nrwl/nx#558b09d7","nrwl/nx#558b09d7","558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\Code.exe","\\Code - Insiders.exe","\\Cursor.exe","\\Codium.exe","\\VSCodium.exe")
    | where CommandLine has_any ("github:nrwl/nx#558b09d7","nrwl/nx#558b09d7","558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("code","cursor","codium","Code Helper","Code - Insiders","Electron")
    | where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("github:nrwl/nx#558b09d7","nrwl/nx#558b09d7","558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Nx Console v18.95.0 Compromised VSIX / main.js / payload SHA-256 Hash Match Installation High
Detects file-system writes, process executions, or image loads matching any of the three SHA-256 hashes published by StepSecurity for the compromised Nx Console artefacts: the VSIX bundle, main.js, and the obfuscated index.js payload. Rationale: The three SHA-256 hashes are published verbatim in the StepSecurity post and corroborated by The Hacker News and GBHackers; a cryptographic hash match is the highest-fidelity primitive available. Hash collisions on SHA-256 are computationally infeasible — any hit on a non-sandbox host is a true positive. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/

[LLM] macOS LaunchAgent Persistence — com.user.kitty-monitor.plist (Nx Console Compromise) Installation High
Detects creation of the LaunchAgent plist `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist` — the macOS persistence mechanism dropped by the Nx Console v18.95.0 obfuscated payload to keep the credential-stealer running across logins. Rationale: The exact filename `com.user.kitty-monitor.plist` under `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` is published in the StepSecurity IOC list and corroborated by The Hacker News write-up. It is a unique persistence artefact — no legitimate macOS software uses this bundle identifier — making any file-create event on this path a true positive. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1547
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/" or FolderPath has @"\Library\LaunchAgents\"
| where FileName =~ "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist" or FolderPath endswith "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileCreate")
| where TargetFilePath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/"
| where TargetFileName =~ "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist" or TargetFilePath endswith "com.user.kitty-monitor.plist"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Kitty cat.py Python Backdoor File Drop / Execution (Nx Console Compromise) Installation High
Detects creation of `~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py` or execution of a python interpreter referencing that path or `/tmp/kitty-*` — the Linux/macOS Python backdoor stage dropped by the Nx Console v18.95.0 obfuscated payload. Rationale: The path `~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py` and `/tmp/kitty-*` directories are published verbatim in the StepSecurity IOC list and corroborated by The Hacker News and GBHackers. The `kitty` directory under user-local share is unrelated to the legitimate Kitty terminal (which uses `~/.config/kitty/`) — there is no benign use of this exact path, making it high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/

[LLM] AWS IMDS (169.254.169.254) Hit from Developer / Non-EC2 Endpoint (Nx Console Credential Theft) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects outbound connections to the AWS Instance Metadata Service (169.254.169.254) from endpoints that are not EC2 instances. The Nx Console v18.95.0 payload probes IMDS to steal IAM role credentials — a developer laptop or non-AWS workstation contacting IMDS is a strong credential-access signal. Rationale: The article and external corroboration (The Hacker News, CyberSecurityNews, GBHackers) call out `Connections to AWS IMDS (169.254.169.254) from non-AWS environments` as a documented IOC of the Nx Console payload's credential-stealing stage. The 169.254.169.254 link-local address has only one legitimate use (EC2/IMDS); any hit from a Mac/Linux laptop or developer workstation is anomalous. Sigma is omitted because the detection requires asset-class context (non-EC2) that single-event Sigma cannot express cleanly. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised/ • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1078.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let DevEndpoints = DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, DeviceCategory, OSPlatform, DeviceType, IsInternetFacing) by DeviceId, DeviceName
    | where DeviceCategory != "Server" or isempty(DeviceCategory);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
| where RemotePort in (80,443,8080)
| join kind=inner DevEndpoints on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, DeviceCategory, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254"
| where DstPortNumber in (80,443,8080)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkBytes, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd OR source:linux.syslog OR source:osquery) (@DestinationIp:169.254.169.254 OR @network.destination.ip:169.254.169.254 OR @DestinationHostname:*169.254.169.254*) -@host.tags:cloud_provider\:aws
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="169.254.169.254" RemotePort=/^(80|443|8080)$/ | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.src_ip) as src_ip values(All_Traffic.app) as app values(All_Traffic.process_name) as process_name values(All_Traffic.user) as user from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_ip="169.254.169.254" AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (80,443,8080) NOT (All_Traffic.src_category IN ("aws-ec2","aws_instance","ec2")) by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where count > 0 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.src_ip) as src_ip values(All_Traffic.app) as app values(All_Traffic.process_name) as process_name values(All_Traffic.user) as user from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_ip="169.254.169.254" AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (80,443,8080) NOT (All_Traffic.src_category IN ("aws-ec2","aws_instance","ec2")) by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where count > 0 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]

[LLM] FlutterShell macOS C2 contact (atsheisdomestic / etoftheappyrince / healightejustb) Command & Control High
Detects endpoint contact to the three FlutterShell variant-specific C2 domains catalogued by Unit 42 for the PodcastsLounge, PDF-Brain, and PDF-Ninja variants. Hits represent post-installation backdoor check-in, not adware redirect. Rationale: Three C2 domains are listed in the Unit 42 variant matrix (Table 2) — single-purpose attacker infrastructure with no legitimate traffic; cross-checked against the Unit 42 report. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/flutterbridge-new-fluttershell-backdoor/ • https://cyberpress.org/jscorerunner-malware/ • https://gbhackers.com/new-mac-malware/

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,

[LLM] FlutterShell macOS payload SHA256 IOC match Installation High
Hashes any binary write or execution against the 8 SHA256 indicators Unit 42 published for the three FlutterShell variant builds. Catches the malware itself regardless of bundle name, since the actor has signed multiple Developer ID identities. Rationale: Eight SHA256s explicitly published by Unit 42 across PodcastsLounge, PDF-Brain, and PDF-Ninja variants. Hash IOC matching has near-zero FP outside of analyst sandboxes — high alerting fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/flutterbridge-new-fluttershell-backdoor/

[LLM] Non-Chrome process modifies macOS Chrome Preferences (FlutterShell browser hijack) Actions on Objectives Medium
Catches the FlutterShell adware stage where the malware rewrites ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Preferences (and Secure Preferences / Local State) to force traffic through the attacker-controlled redirector. Chrome itself is the only normal writer of these files on macOS. Rationale: Article explicitly states FlutterShell 'modifies Google Chrome configuration files to hijack the browser' — the three macOS Chrome state files are the documented hijack targets and Chrome itself is the only normal writer. Pivoting on InitiatingProcessFileName surfaces the Flutter binary by name. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/flutterbridge-new-fluttershell-backdoor/
ATT&CKT1176 T1539 T1185
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FolderPath contains "/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/"
| where FileName in ("Preferences","Secure Preferences","Local State")
| where ActionType in ("FileModified","FileCreated")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("Google Chrome","Google Chrome Helper","Google Chrome Helper (Renderer)","Google Chrome Helper (GPU)","chrome","chrome_crashpad_handler")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "jamf" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "intune" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("managedsoftwareupdate","munki")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetFilePath has "/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/"
| where TargetFileName in ("Preferences","Secure Preferences","Local State")
| where EventType in ("FileModified","FileCreated","FileWritten")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("Google Chrome","Google Chrome Helper","Google Chrome Helper (Renderer)","Google Chrome Helper (GPU)","chrome","chrome_crashpad_handler")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !contains "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Non-Chrome Process Writing macOS Chrome Preferences (FlutterShell Browser Hijack)
id: 2c5e9a13-b6f4-49d2-9e8b-4f2a1c7d3b08
description: Detects modification of Google Chrome Preferences / Secure Preferences / Local State on macOS by a process other than Chrome itself. FlutterShell rewrites these files to force browser traffic through ads-parkpro / softwe.art redirectors.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/flutterbridge-new-fluttershell-backdoor/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/02
tags:
  - attack.t1176
  - attack.t1185
  - attack.t1539
  - attack.impact
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: macos
detection:
  target_files:
    TargetFilename|contains: '/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '/Preferences'
      - '/Secure Preferences'
      - '/Local State'
  filter_chrome:
    Image|contains: '/Google Chrome.app/Contents/'
  condition: target_files and not filter_chrome
falsepositives:
  - MDM-pushed Chrome enterprise policy writes (Jamf, Intune, Workspace ONE)
  - User-driven Chrome profile reset utilities
level: medium
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| regex("/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/", field=TargetFileName)
| TargetFileName=/(Preferences|Secure Preferences|Local State)$/
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\/Google Chrome\.app\/Contents\/.+\/(Google Chrome|Google Chrome Helper.*|chrome_crashpad_handler|chrome)$/)
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/(jamf|munki|managedsoftwareupdate|intune)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=[count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])

[LLM] FlutterShell adware redirector contact (ads-parkpro / sinterfumesco / softwe.art) Actions on Objectives High
Detects endpoint contact to the five adware-redirector domains the FlutterShell campaign funnels hijacked browser traffic through. Distinct from the C2 detection — these surface the in-the-wild adware stage and may catch hosts where the C2 has rotated. Rationale: Five redirector domains listed in the Unit 42 IOC bundle as the ad-filled intermediary destinations. Catching them complements the C2 detection (which fires post-install) by catching the visible browser-hijack symptom, which often persists even after the C2 rotates. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/flutterbridge-new-fluttershell-backdoor/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.008
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
let Redirectors = dynamic(["sinterfumesco.com","ads-parkpro.com","adsparkpro.top","adsparkpro.net","softwe.art"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (Redirectors)
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".sinterfumesco.com"
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".ads-parkpro.com"
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".adsparkpro.top"
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".adsparkpro.net"
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".softwe.art"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let Redirectors = dynamic(["sinterfumesco.com","ads-parkpro.com","adsparkpro.top","adsparkpro.net","softwe.art"]);
let dnsHits = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (Redirectors)
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url=DnsQuery, EventVendor, EventProduct;
let webHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (Redirectors) or HttpHostName has_any (Redirectors)
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, EventVendor, EventProduct;
union dnsHits, webHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688

| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"

status: experimental
description: |

    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bbd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745") or SHA1 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bbd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745") or MD5 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bbd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bbd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745") or SHA1 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bbd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745") or MD5 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bbd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bbd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Pakistan-Linked SideCopy Targets Afghanistan Finance Ministry with Xeno RAT

The Hacker News
2026-06-02 15 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a spear-phishing campaign likely undertaken by the Pakistan-aligned SideCopy group targeting Afghanistan's Ministry of Finance with an open-source remote access trojan called Xeno RAT. "The campaign opens with a spear phishing delivery - a ZIP archive containing a malicious LNK file bearing a carefully crafted Pashto-language filename,"

[LLM] SideCopy LNK-via-ZIP spawning mshta.exe with remote HTA URL Delivery High
Detects the Operation XENOFISCAL initial-access stage where a Pashto-named .LNK inside a ZIP is double-clicked from explorer.exe and invokes mshta.exe with a remote URL argument to stage Xeno RAT. The parent=explorer + child=mshta + remote-URL combination is the article's specific entry pattern. Rationale: Article-specific: SideCopy's Operation XENOFISCAL chain explicitly states the .LNK opens via mshta.exe to fetch a remote .hta. The parent=explorer/archiver + child=mshta + URL arg is a high-signal triad and matches the Seqrite report's step 1. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1008/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/005/
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002 T1218.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "mshta.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","winrar.exe","7zg.exe","7zfm.exe","winzip64.exe","winzip32.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://",".hta")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\mshta.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\winrar.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\7zg.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\7zfm.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\winzip64.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\winzip32.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("http://","https://",".hta")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName

[LLM] Xeno RAT staging — mshta/wscript fetching HTA from abimj.edu.af Delivery High
Detects the second-stage delivery in Operation XENOFISCAL where mshta.exe (or other LOLBins) reaches out to the compromised Afghan education domain abimj.edu.af to retrieve the obfuscated JavaScript HTA dropper. Pivots on the article's named C2/staging domain in both process command-line and network telemetry. Rationale: abimj.edu.af is explicitly named by Seqrite as the compromised Afghan education domain that hosts the HTA payload. A single fully-qualified-domain match is high-fidelity, near-zero-FP, and covers DNS, proxy, and EDR pivot points. Cross-checked against MITRE G1008 (Transparent Tribe/SideCopy) profile. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1008/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/pakistan-linked-sidecopy-targets.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1218.005 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let staging_domain = "abimj.edu.af";
let proc = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has staging_domain or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has staging_domain
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="Process";
let net = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
    | where RemoteUrl has staging_domain
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=tostring(RemoteUrl), Source="Network";
proc
| union net
| order by Timestamp desc
let staging_domain = "abimj.edu.af";
union isfuzzy=true
  (SecurityEvent
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
     | where EventID == 4688
     | where CommandLine has staging_domain
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="Process"),
  (DnsEvents
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
     | where Name endswith staging_domain
     | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType=QueryTypeName, ResultCode=tostring(ResultCode), Source="DNS"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
     | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
     | where RequestURL has staging_domain or DestinationHostName has staging_domain
     | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL, DestinationHostName, DeviceVendor, Source="Proxy")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
